To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The 5382InsC mutation in BRAC1 was found in eleven families and the 9613delC mutation in BRA2 occurred in three.
1. The most frequent BRCA1 and 2 mutations in Poland are the 5382ins and 9631del mutations.

the 5382ins C and 9631del C mutations are the major cause of breast/ovarian cancers in Polish families, and that the 1095del 8 mutation in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene is the largest germin deletion in coding sequence identified thus far.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of disease predisposing mutations of the TP53, BRCA1, and BRCA2 gene in families with breast and/or ovarian cancer from Upper Silesia.
the identification of mutations in BRCA genes and TP53 gene in families with breast and/or ovarian cancer.
the identification of the genetic cause of familial breast/ovarian cancers in the Polish population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in Upper Silesian families with a history of breast and ovarian cancers, the frequency of germ line mutations in BRCA genes is high and that the two most frequent BRCA1 and 2 mutations are common in the Polish population.

the frequency of germ line mutations in BRCA 1 and BRCA 2 genes in Polish high risk families is similar to that in other populations, and the 5382insc and 9631delc mutations are the most frequent mutations in Polish families with high risk for breast cancer.
the frequency of mutations in BRCA2 is higher in Poland than in other populations, and that BRCA1 and TP53 mutations occur with similar frequency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most common mutations in BRCA2 and TP53 genes were found in the same region of Poland, Upper Silesia.

36% of the breast/ovarian Polish cancer families investigated in this study carry a mutation in BRCA genes, and that 30% of these families carry either the 5382ins C mutation in BRCA 1 or the 9631 del C mutation in BRAC2.
the frequency of BRCA1 and 2 mutations in Polish families with familial breast and ovarian cancer is similar to that observed in high-risk families from other populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5382ins C mutation is the most frequent BRCA1 mutation in Polish breast/ovarian families, while the 9631 del C mutation in BRCA 2 is the second most frequent mutation in this group of families.
a high proportion of Polish breast/ovarian families carry BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutations and that these families should be tested for common mutations.
the 5382insc and 9631delc mutations are very frequent in Polish breast cancer families, and that they should be screened for in all Polish breast cancer families.
